findings.title: Review synchronization serializes up to hundreds of individually timed requests
findings.where: src/lib/github-review-sync.ts:486 and src/lib/github-review-sync.ts:501; repository iteration is also serial at src/lib/github-review-sync.ts:523-533.
findings.what: Each pull request timeline fetch is awaited before the next begins. With the defaults, 100 timeline requests can each consume the 5-second timeout, producing roughly 500 seconds of ingest latency; configuration permits up to 10,000 requests. The request-count bound prevents infinity but supplies no total latency budget.
findings.fix: Fetch timelines with a small bounded concurrency pool and impose a total synchronization deadline; preserve the existing record and request ceilings.
findings.acceptance: Using a fake fetch that delays every timeline response, verify multiple timeline requests overlap only up to the configured concurrency and the entire sync aborts or returns fallback data within a fixed total deadline substantially below requestCount × fetchTimeoutMs.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the inner loop awaits fetchJsonArray at line 501 and the outer repository loop awaits each repository at lines 527-533. Existing tests cap call count but provide no total-duration guard.

findings.title: Sparse hook timings are misrepresented as overhead on every turn
findings.what: The input is explicitly the mean over only the timed subset, and the module notes duration is present on approximately 7% of fires. Nevertheless, generated prose says the measured mean applies to every turn and is paid on every turn. Untimed turns provide no evidence for that extrapolation.
findings.fix: Describe the value as the mean among timed Stop events and remove the universal per-turn statements unless the input also supplies total turns and evidence establishing coverage.
findings.acceptance: For a measured mean of 5000 ms over 10 timed events, the corrective states that the mean covers the timed subset and contains neither 'every turn' nor an equivalent universal claim; update the unit test accordingly.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read both the telemetry provenance and emitted strings. Lines 31-36 define subset-only evidence, while lines 62-71 extrapolate it universally; the test at lines 16-23 deliberately locks in that extrapolation.

findings.title: Hybrid search rebuilds and sorts the entire corpus on every query
findings.what: For every query, every eligible entry concatenates all pasted content, tokenizes it, allocates a new vector, calculates similarity, creates a result object and snippet, and then sorts the complete match set before taking at most 100 results. Cost scales with total transcript bytes on each invocation and can stall an interactive search surface or create large transient allocations.
findings.fix: Precompute/cache normalized entry text and semantic vectors when the dataset changes, cap indexed text per entry, and retain only the top K matches without sorting the full result set.
findings.acceptance: Add a representative large-corpus performance probe with a documented latency and memory budget; repeated queries over an unchanged corpus must not rebuild entry vectors, and pasted-content size must be explicitly bounded.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed there is no precomputed index or early limit: entryText includes every pasted-content value, embedSearchText runs inside the per-entry map, and slice(limit) occurs only after full filtering and sorting.
